title: The Radio Repairer
audience: REPLACE: e.g. my cousins and siblings, 18-35, watching on phones; Ethiopian family members at home and in the diaspora
intent: REPLACE: e.g. by the end they feel pride in my father's patience and remember the proverb he repeats
style_block: warm hand-painted illustration, soft grain, golden-hour light, muted ochre and teal palette, gentle film texture, subject centred in frame

character.name: Abebe
character.description: an Ethiopian man in his thirties in the 1980s, short black hair, thin moustache, white cotton shirt with rolled sleeves, calm focused eyes
character.reference_prompt: character reference sheet, front view, side view and three-quarter view of the same man, neutral background

models.tts_style: Read slowly, in a calm, warm, unhurried storytelling voice:

shots.reason: Establishing shot: tells the viewer where and when the story happens.
shots.image_prompt: a small Ethiopian town street at dawn in the 1980s, tin-roof shops, eucalyptus trees, mountains behind
shots.motion_prompt: the camera pushes in slowly, smoke drifts from a chimney
shots.subtitle_en: In our town, every morning began with a radio.

shots.reason: Introduces the main character in his place of work.
shots.image_prompt: the man sitting behind a wooden counter in a tiny repair shop full of old radios
shots.motion_prompt: he looks up and smiles gently, fixed camera
shots.subtitle_en: My father fixed them in a shop no wider than a door.

shots.reason: Close detail that shows the skill and patience of the work.
shots.image_prompt: close-up of hands holding a small screwdriver over the open back of a vintage radio, glowing valves
shots.motion_prompt: the screwdriver turns slowly, warm light flickers
shots.subtitle_en: He learned by opening what others threw away.

shots.reason: Shows the community depending on him; widens the stakes.
shots.image_prompt: neighbours queueing outside the tiny shop holding radios wrapped in cloth
shots.motion_prompt: the camera pans slowly right along the queue
shots.subtitle_en: Soon the whole street brought him their voices to mend.

shots.reason: The turning point: a problem he cannot solve quickly.
shots.image_prompt: the man frowning at a broken radio late at night under a single bulb
shots.motion_prompt: he leans closer, the bulb sways a little
shots.subtitle_en: One night a radio would not speak, however he tried.

shots.reason: Carries the emotional core: the proverb he lives by.
shots.image_prompt: close-up of the man's calm face, eyes closed, taking a slow breath
shots.motion_prompt: he breathes in slowly, fixed camera
shots.subtitle_en: He said: slowly, slowly, the egg will walk on its own legs.

shots.image_prompt: the radio's dial lighting up amber in a dark room
shots.motion_prompt: the dial glow brightens, the camera pushes in

shots.reason: Bridges past to present; the motif returns.
shots.image_prompt: the same old radio on a shelf in a modern living room, sunlight through a window
shots.motion_prompt: the camera pulls back slowly, dust floats in the sunlight
shots.subtitle_en: That radio still sits in our house today.

shots.reason: Ending: hands the lesson to the next generation, the audience.
shots.image_prompt: a young person's hands turning the dial of the old radio, warm morning light
shots.motion_prompt: the fingers turn the dial gently, the camera pushes in
shots.subtitle_en: And when things go wrong, I hear him: slowly, slowly.

music.caption: instrumental, gentle Ethiopian tizita-inspired score, soft krar plucks, warm pads, slow, nostalgic, sparse texture, no strong lead melody

cues.description: theme returns, warmth builds to the end

end_card.text: Made with AI: Gemini TTS, FLUX, Wan 2.2, ACE-Step
